extracted.intended_audience: citizens, public officials, legislators, and legal practitioners concerned with the State Constitution of North Carolina
extracted.subtask_description: Text of constitutional provisions setting out the organization, powers, duties, qualifications, and limits of the legislative, executive, judicial, fiscal, suffrage, municipal, corporate, educational, and homestead rules for the State of North Carolina.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative compensation limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the General Assembly shall receive four dollars per day for each day of their session for a period not exceeding sixty days; if they remain longer they shall serve without compensation; mileage of ten cents per mile to be computed by nearest line of public travel; presiding officers receive six dollars per day and mileage; extra sessions compensated at same rate for up to twenty days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies daily pay caps, mileage calculation, and caps on compensated duration of regular and extra sessions; no compensation beyond stated limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Department composition and term
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Department shall consist of a Governor, Lieutenant Governor, Secretary of State, Auditor, Treasurer, Superintendent of Public Instruction, and Attorney-General, who shall be elected for a term of four years by qualified electors at the same time and in the same manner as members of the General Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term commences January 1 after election and continues until successors are elected and qualified; first officers assume duties ten days after approval by U.S. Congress and hold office four years from after the first day of January.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governor and Lieutenant-Governor eligibility and term limits
rubrics_metrics.description: No person shall be eligible as Governor or Lieutenant-Governor unless he shall have attained the age of thirty years, shall have been a citizen of the United States five years, and shall have been a resident of this State for two years next before the election; nor shall the person elected to either of these offices be eligible to the same office more than four years in any term of eight years, unless the office shall have been cast upon him as Lieutenant-Governor or President of the Senate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets age, citizenship, residency qualifications and a term-limit safeguard for the two highest executive offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return and certification of executive elections
rubrics_metrics.description: The return of every election for officers of the Executive Department shall be sealed and transmitted to the seat of government to the Speaker of the House of Representatives, who shall open and publish them before a majority of both Houses; persons having the highest number of votes declared duly elected; ties chosen by joint ballot of both Houses; contested elections determined by joint ballot as prescribed by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes legislative role in certifying and resolving ties or contested elections for executive officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive oath of office
rubrics_metrics.description: The Governor, before entering upon the duties of his office, shall, in the presence of both branches of the General Assembly, or before any Justice of the Supreme Court, take an oath or affirmation to support the U.S. and State constitutions and to faithfully perform the duties of Governor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies where and the substance of the oath required before assuming duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governor's duty to inform and recommend
rubrics_metrics.description: The Governor shall reside at the seat of government and shall, from time to time, give the General Assembly information of the affairs of the State and recommend measures he shall deem expedient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes an informational and advisory duty on the Governor toward the legislature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pardons, reprieves, and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Governor shall have power to grant reprieves, commutations and pardons after conviction (except in cases of impeachment), upon such conditions as he may think proper and subject to regulations by law regarding application for pardons; he shall biennially communicate each case to the General Assembly with name, crime, sentence/date, commutation/pardon date, and reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants clemency powers but requires periodic reporting with specified details to the legislature; subject to statutory regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive reports and duty to ensure execution of laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers of the Executive Department and public institutions shall report to the Governor at least five days prior to each regular session, who shall transmit such reports with his message to the General Assembly; the Governor may require information in writing from executive officers and shall take care that the laws be faithfully executed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates reporting obligations for executive officers and empowers the Governor to demand written information and ensure enforcement of laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governor as Commander-in-Chief
rubrics_metrics.description: The Governor shall be Commander-in-Chief of the militia of the State, except when they shall be called into the service of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines military command role subject to federal call.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to convene extra sessions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Governor shall have power, on extraordinary occasions, by and with the advice of the Council of State, to convene the General Assembly into extra session by proclamation, stating the purpose or purposes for which they are convened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows special convocations limited to stated purposes and requiring Council of State advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive appointment powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Governor shall nominate and, by and with the advice and consent of a majority of the Senators elect, appoint all officers whose offices are established by this Constitution and whose appointments are not otherwise provided for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes appointment process requiring Senate consent for constitutional offices not otherwise provided for.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lieutenant-Governor duties and compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lieutenant-Governor shall be President of the Senate, with no vote unless the Senate is equally divided; while acting as President of the Senate he receives the same pay as the Speaker of the House for the same period and no other compensation except when acting as Governor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits voting power and prescribes compensation parity with Speaker when presiding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Succession and acting Governor provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases of impeachment, failure to qualify, absence, inability, or vacancy in the office of Governor, the powers, duties and emoluments shall devolve upon the Lieutenant-Governor until disabilities cease or a new Governor is elected and qualified; if Lieutenant-Governor unable to preside, Senators elect a President of their body who shall assume gubernatorial duties as acting Governor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines hierarchical succession and temporary assumption of duties, including procedures during recess requiring Secretary of State to convene the Senate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties and filling vacancies for other executive officers
rubrics_metrics.description: The respective duties of the Secretary of State, Auditor, Treasurer, Superintendent of Public Instruction and Attorney-General shall be prescribed by law; if an office becomes vacant it is the duty of the Governor to appoint another until disability removed or successor elected; every such vacancy to be filled by election at the first general election more than thirty days after the vacancy, with the person chosen to hold for the remainder of the unexpired term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines statutory duty-setting with gubernatorial interim appointment and subsequent election rules for vacancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council of State composition and recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of State, Auditor, Treasurer and Superintendent of Public Instruction shall constitute, ex officio, the Council of State to advise the Governor; three constitute a quorum; their advice and proceedings shall be entered in a journal signed by members, with dissent entries available, and the journal placed before the General Assembly upon request; the Attorney-General shall be ex officio legal adviser to the Executive Department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates an advisory council with formal minutes and dissent entries; sets quorum and advisory legal counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation protection for executive officers
rubrics_metrics.description: The officers mentioned shall, at stated periods, receive compensation established by law which shall neither be increased nor diminished during the time for which they have been elected, and they shall receive no other emolument or allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects salary stability during term and forbids other emoluments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Great Seal custody and use
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be a State seal kept by the Governor called 'the Great Seal of the State of North Carolina'; all grants and commissions shall be entered in the name and by the authority of the State, sealed with the Great Seal, signed by the Governor and countersigned by the Secretary of State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies custody and formal use of the State seal for official acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Agriculture and encouragement of sheep husbandry
rubrics_metrics.description: The General Assembly shall establish a Department of Agriculture, Immigration and Statistics under regulations to promote agricultural interests and enact laws for the adequate protection and encouragement of sheep husbandry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates creation of agricultural administrative structure and legislative protection for specific agricultural industries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abolition of law/equity distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: The distinctions between actions at law and suits in equity and the forms of such actions and suits shall be abolished; there shall be one form of action denominated a civil action; prosecutions by the people shall be termed criminal actions; feigned issues abolished, facts to be tried by order of Court before a jury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unifies procedural forms into civil and criminal actions and eliminates feigned issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial structure and vested power
rubrics_metrics.description: Judicial power vested in a Court for the trial of Impeachments, a Supreme Court, Superior Courts, Courts of Justices of the Peace, and other inferior courts as may be established by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the architecture of the state's judiciary and leaves room for legislative creation of inferior courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial of impeachments and penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court for the trial of impeachments shall be the Senate with a majority quorum; judgment shall not extend beyond removal from and disqualification to hold office in the State; the party remains liable to indictment and punishment according to law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines Senate's role in impeachment trials and limits on impeachment remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: House power to impeach and conviction threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: The House of Representatives exclusively shall have the power of impeaching; no person shall be convicted without concurrence of two-thirds of Senators present; when the Governor is impeached, the Chief-Justice shall preside.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies impeachment initiation and required supermajority for conviction and presiding officer when Governor impeached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treason definition and convicting evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Treason against the State consists only in levying war against it or adhering to its enemies, giving them aid and comfort; no conviction except on testimony of two witnesses to the same overt act or confession in open court; no conviction of treason or attainder shall work corruption of blood or forfeiture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrow statutory definition of treason and high evidentiary standard to convict; forbids corruption of blood or forfeitures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supreme Court composition and jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supreme Court shall consist of a Chief-Justice and two Associate Justices; terms held in Raleigh until otherwise provided; it shall have jurisdiction to review upon appeal any decision of the courts below upon any matter of law or legal inference; jurisdiction over issues/questions of fact shall be as exercised before the 1868 Constitution; Court may issue remedial writs for general supervision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets small bench composition, central sitting place, broad appellate jurisdiction on legal questions, continuity on factual jurisdiction, and remedial writ powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original jurisdiction for claims against the State
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supreme Court shall have original jurisdiction to hear claims against the State, but its decisions shall be merely recommendatory; no execution shall issue; they shall be reported to the next General Assembly for action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows advisory/recommendatory relief on state-claims but actual enforcement deferred to legislature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial districts and Superior Court schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: State divided into nine judicial districts, for each a Judge chosen; Superior Court to be held in each county at least twice a year for times prescribed by law; General Assembly may alter the number of districts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structures trial courts geographically and prescribes minimum sitting frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residence and rotation requirements for Superior Court judges
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Judge of the Superior Court shall reside in the district for which he is elected; Judges shall preside in different districts successively but no Judge shall hold Courts in the same district oftener than once in four years, subject to Governor-mandated replacements for illness or unavoidable accidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes residency requirement and a rotation rule with exception procedures for temporary reassignment by Governor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative limits on altering judicial powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The General Assembly shall have no power to deprive the Judicial Department of any power or jurisdiction rightfully pertaining to it as a coordinate department, but shall allot and distribute that portion not pertaining to the Supreme Court among other courts and provide a proper system of appeals and procedural regulations consistent with the Constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects judicial independence while permitting allocation of lower-court jurisdiction and procedural regulation by legislature, subject to constitutional limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of jury in issues of fact
rubrics_metrics.description: In all issues of fact joined in any court, parties may waive the right to jury; finding of the Judge upon the facts shall have the force and effect of a verdict by a jury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits bench determination of facts by mutual waiver of jury trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of Special Courts for misdemeanors
rubrics_metrics.description: The General Assembly shall provide for the establishment of Special Courts for trial of misdemeanors in cities and towns where necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizes creation of local misdemeanor courts as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerk of Supreme Court appointment and term
rubrics_metrics.description: The Clerk of the Supreme Court shall be appointed by the Court and shall hold office for eight years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies appointing authority and fixed term length for Supreme Court clerk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerk of Superior Court election and term
rubrics_metrics.description: A Clerk of the Superior Court for each county shall be elected by the qualified voters at times and manner prescribed by law and shall hold office for four years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates electoral selection and term length for county clerks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation of fees, salaries and emoluments
rubrics_metrics.description: The General Assembly shall prescribe and regulate the fees, salaries and emoluments of all officers provided for in this Article; but the salaries of Judges shall not be diminished during their continuance in office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislature controls compensation subject to judicial salary protection during term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity of pre-existing laws
rubrics_metrics.description: The laws of North Carolina, not repugnant to this Constitution or the U.S. Constitution and laws, shall be in force until lawfully altered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides continuity of statutory law unless inconsistent with the new Constitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition rules for pending actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions at law and suits in equity pending when Constitution goes into effect shall be transferred to the courts having jurisdiction without prejudice due to the change; cases commenced before adoption of rules of practice and procedure shall be heard according to current practice unless otherwise provided by new rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures orderly transfer and determination of pending cases during procedural changeover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election and term of Justices and Superior Court judges
rubrics_metrics.description: Justices of the Supreme Court shall be elected by qualified voters and hold office for eight years; Judges of the Superior Courts elected at the first election under this amendment shall be elected in like manner and hold office for eight years; General Assembly may later provide for district-based elections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes popular election of higher court judges and eight-year terms with potential later modification for district elections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Superior Courts availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Superior Courts shall be at all times open for transaction of all business within their jurisdiction, except the trial of issues of fact requiring a jury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates continuity of court availability subject to jury-case exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitor election and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: A Solicitor shall be elected for each Judicial District by qualified voters to hold office for four years, prosecute on behalf of the State in all criminal actions in the Superior Courts and advise officers of justice in his district.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines prosecutorial office, election, term and duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local law-enforcement officer elections and terms
rubrics_metrics.description: In each county a Sheriff and Coroner shall be elected by qualified voters and hold office for two years; in each township a Constable elected in like manner holds office for two years; when no Coroner exists the Clerk may appoint one for special cases; county Commissioners may appoint to fill vacancies for unexpired term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides electoral selection, term lengths, and vacancy-appointment procedures for local officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filling vacancies in offices
rubrics_metrics.description: All vacancies occurring in offices provided by this Article shall be filled by appointments of the Governor unless otherwise provided; appointees hold until next regular election for General Assembly members when elections shall fill such offices; incumbents hold until successors are qualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates gubernatorial interim appointment power and requirement that successors be elected at next regular election, with incumbents continuing until successors qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional timing for officers elected under new Constitution
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers elected at the first election under this Constitution shall hold their offices for the terms prescribed next ensuing after the next regular election for members of the General Assembly; their terms begin upon approval of this Constitution by U.S. Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governs commencement and sequencing of initial terms after constitutional adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction and procedures for Justices of the Peace
rubrics_metrics.description: Justices of the Peace shall have jurisdiction, under regulations by the General Assembly, of civil actions founded on contract where sum demanded does not exceed $200 and title to real estate not in controversy; criminal matters where punishment cannot exceed $50 fine or 30 days imprisonment; General Assembly may extend civil jurisdiction up to $50 in other cases; jury of six men summoned on demand; appeals to Superior Court permitted; Justice must record proceedings and file with Clerk of Superior Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines small-claims thresholds, criminal limits, jury procedures and appeal/record-keeping duties for Justices of the Peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vacancy appointment procedures for Justices and Clerks
rubrics_metrics.description: When Justice of the Peace office becomes vacant otherwise than by term expiration or failure to elect, Clerk of Superior Court shall appoint to fill vacancy for unexpired term; if Clerk's office becomes vacant otherwise than by expiration or failure to elect, Judge of Superior Court shall appoint until an election can be regularly held.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies local appointment authorities for different types of vacancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election/term provisions for presiding officers of newly established inferior courts
rubrics_metrics.description: If General Assembly establishes other courts inferior to the Supreme Court, the presiding officers and clerks thereof shall be elected in such manner as the General Assembly may prescribe and shall hold offices for a term not exceeding eight years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives legislature flexibility to set selection methods and term limits up to eight years for officers of newly created courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of judges and presiding officers for inability
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Judge of the Supreme Court or of the Superior Courts, and presiding officers of such inferior courts, may be removed from office for mental or physical inability upon a concurrent resolution of two-thirds of both Houses of the General Assembly; the person shall receive notice with causes alleged at least twenty days before action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides removal mechanism for incapacity with notice and supermajority legislative concurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of court clerks for inability and appeal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Clerk of the Supreme Court or of the Superior Courts or inferior courts may be removed for mental or physical inability: Clerk of Supreme Court by the Judges; Clerks of Superior Courts by the Judge riding the district; clerks of inferior courts by presiding officers; Clerk shall receive notice with causes at least ten days before action and is entitled to appeal to next term of Superior Court and thence to Supreme Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies removal authorities, notice periods, and appellate rights for clerks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-vacation of existing offices by amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments made to the Constitution by this Convention shall not have effect to vacate any office or term of office now existing under the Constitution of the State and filled or held by virtue of any election or appointment under said Constitution and laws made in pursuance thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects continuity of existing office-holders from being vacated by constitutional amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitation (poll) tax and exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: General Assembly shall levy a capitation tax on every male inhabitant over 21 and under 50 equal to the tax on property valued at $300; county commissioners may exempt in special cases for poverty and infirmity; combined State and county capitation tax shall never exceed two dollars on the head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets poll tax base, possible exemptions, and maximum combined rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of capitation tax proceeds
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceeds of State and county capitation tax shall be applied to the purposes of education and the support of the poor, but not more than 25% in any one year may be appropriated to support of the poor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dedicates poll tax revenue primarily to education with a specified cap on poor relief allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform taxation of monies, credits and property
rubrics_metrics.description: Laws shall be passed taxing, by a uniform rule, all moneys, credits, investments in bonds, stocks, joint-stock companies or otherwise, and all real and personal property according to true value in money; General Assembly may also tax trades, professions, franchises and incomes provided no income taxed when underlying property already taxed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates uniformity in taxation across classes of property and financial assets and restricts double taxation of income when property is taxed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on State indebtedness and lending credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Until State bonds are at par, General Assembly shall have no power to contract new debt except to supply casual deficit or for suppressing invasion or insurrection unless same bill levies a special tax to pay interest annually; General Assembly shall have no power to give or lend State credit to persons/associations/corporations except to aid completion of unfinished railroads in which State has direct pecuniary interest unless submitted to popular vote and approved by majority of voters who vote on it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restricts borrowing and use of State credit, with narrow exceptions and requirement of concomitant taxation or popular approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax exemptions for State and certain properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Property belonging to the State or municipal corporations shall be exempt from taxation; General Assembly may exempt cemeteries and property held for educational, scientific, literary, charitable or religious purposes, wearing apparel, arms for muster, household and kitchen furniture, mechanical and agricultural implements, libraries and scientific instruments, or any other personal property to a value not exceeding $300.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists exempt categories and a monetary cap for personal property exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: County tax limits and levy object requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Taxes levied by county commissioners shall be levied like State taxes and shall never exceed double the State taxes except for special purpose with General Assembly approval; every act levying a tax shall state the special object to which it is to be applied and it shall be applied to no other purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caps county taxation relative to State rate and requires earmarking of tax acts to specific purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suffrage qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Every male person born in the United States and every naturalized male person twenty-one years old or upward who has resided in the State twelve months preceding the elections and ninety days in the county where he offers to vote shall be an elector; persons convicted or confessed to felony or other infamous crime shall not be electors unless restored to rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines voter eligibility by citizenship, age, and residency, and disqualifies felons unless restored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voter registration and oath requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: General Assembly shall provide for registration of all electors; no person shall vote without registration or register without first taking an oath or affirmation to support and maintain the U.S. and North Carolina Constitutions and laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes mandatory registration and an oath prerequisite to registering to vote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ballot and viva voce rule
rubrics_metrics.description: All elections by the people shall be by ballot, and all elections by the General Assembly shall be viva voce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiates secret ballot for popular elections and voice vote for legislative elections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to office and required oath
rubrics_metrics.description: Every voter (except as provided) shall be eligible to office; before entering duties he shall take an oath to support and maintain the U.S. and State Constitutions and to faithfully discharge duties of his office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links voter status to office eligibility and prescribes the form of the official oath.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disqualifications for office
rubrics_metrics.description: Classes disqualified: (1) All persons who shall deny the being of Almighty God. (2) All persons convicted of treason, perjury, or any other infamous crime since becoming citizens of the U.S., or of corruption or malpractice in office, unless legally restored to rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides religious test (denial of God) and criminal/misconduct disqualifications for office-holding.

rubrics_metrics.name: County officer elections and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: In each county there shall be elected biennially by qualified voters a Treasurer, Register of Deeds, Surveyor and five Commissioners; Commissioners exercise general supervision and control of penal and charitable institutions, schools, roads, bridges, levying of taxes and finances of the county as prescribed by law; Register of Deeds shall be ex officio Clerk of the Board of Commissioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies county-level elected offices, their election schedule and principal duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Township creation and governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioners first elected in each county shall divide the same into convenient districts, determine boundaries and names and report to General Assembly before Jan 1, 1869; upon approval by General Assembly the districts shall have corporate powers as townships; in each township biennially elected Clerk and two Justices of the Peace shall constitute a Board of Trustees to control taxes, finances, roads, bridges under County Commissioners' supervision; each township shall elect a School Committee of three persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes local subdivisions (townships) with corporate powers and local governance bodies for administrative and education oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Township trustees' assessment and treasury duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Township Board of Trustees shall assess taxable property of townships and make return to County Commissioners for revision as prescribed by law; Clerk shall be ex officio Treasurer of the township.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigns local assessment and treasury responsibilities to township trustees and clerk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Municipal debt and treasury controls
rubrics_metrics.description: No county, city, town or other municipal corporation shall contract any debt, pledge its faith, or loan its credit, nor shall any tax be levied or collected by officers except for necessary expenses, unless by vote of a majority of qualified voters therein; no money shall be drawn from any county or township treasury except by authority of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restricts municipal borrowing, credit use, taxation and treasury disbursements to voter-approved or lawful necessities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform ad valorem local taxation
rubrics_metrics.description: All taxes levied by any county, city, town or township shall be uniform and ad valorem upon all property in the same, except property exempted by this Constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates uniform assessment and ad valorem basis for local taxation within taxing units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial assumption of duties by county officers
rubrics_metrics.description: The county officers first elected under this Article shall enter upon their duties ten days after approval of this Constitution by the U.S. Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies commencement timing for initial county officeholders following constitutional approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governor's interim appointments of Justices of the Peace
rubrics_metrics.description: The Governor shall appoint a sufficient number of Justices of the Peace in each county who shall hold their places until sections four, five and six of this Article have been carried into effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows temporary gubernatorial appointments to ensure judicial presence until elected structures in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuance of municipal charters and ordinances
rubrics_metrics.description: All charters, ordinances and provisions relating to municipal corporations shall remain in force until legally changed unless inconsistent with provisions of this Constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves existing municipal law subject to constitutional conformity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on municipal payment for rebellion debts
rubrics_metrics.description: No county, city, town or municipal corporation shall assume to pay nor shall any tax be levied or collected for payment of any debt or interest upon any debt contracted directly or indirectly in aid or support of the rebellion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bars use of municipal resources to satisfy debts incurred to support rebellion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative modification power over municipal article
rubrics_metrics.description: The General Assembly shall have full power by statute to modify, change, or abridge any provisions of this Article and substitute others in their place, except sections seven, nine and thirteen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants legislature power to amend most municipal provisions except specified protected sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporation formation and alteration rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporations may be formed under general laws but shall not be created by special act except for municipal purposes and where objects cannot be attained under general laws; all general laws and special acts may be altered or repealed from time to time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires corporations to be formed under general statutes except narrow exceptions and allows legislative revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate liability and definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Dues from corporations shall be secured by such individual liabilities of the corporation and other means as prescribed by law; term corporation includes associations and joint-stock companies having corporate powers and privileges not possessed by individuals or partnerships; corporations have right to sue and be sued in all courts like natural persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines corporate forms, liability security, and legal personhood for litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative duty to provide city/town organization and restrict powers
rubrics_metrics.description: It shall be duty of the Legislature to provide for organization of cities, towns and incorporated villages and to restrict their power of taxation, assessment, borrowing money, contracting debts and loaning credits to prevent abuses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs legislature to regulate municipal organization and constrain fiscal powers to avoid abuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education encouragement principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Religion, morality and knowledge being necessary to good government and happiness of mankind, schools and the means of education shall forever be encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States foundational policy connecting education, religion, morality and civic welfare as a permanent public objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free public school system and racial segregation rule
rubrics_metrics.description: General Assembly shall provide for a general and uniform system of public schools wherein tuition shall be free to all children between ages six and twenty-one; children of the white race and of the colored race shall be taught in separate public schools but there shall be no discrimination in favor of or to the prejudice of either race.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates free universal public education with explicit requirement for separate schools by race while mandating no discrimination between races (reflects historical segregationist framework).

rubrics_metrics.name: County school districts and minimum session length
rubrics_metrics.description: Each county shall be divided into convenient districts maintaining one or more public schools at least four months every year; Commissioners failing to comply shall be liable to indictment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires minimum school session length and imposes criminal liability for officials who fail to provide mandated schooling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedicated educational funding sources and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceeds of U.S.-granted lands not otherwise appropriated, state educational funds, net proceeds of swamp land sales and other grants/gifts shall be paid into State treasury and, with ordinary revenue set apart by law, faithfully appropriated for establishing and maintaining free public schools and for no other uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates constitutionally dedicated educational revenue streams and forbids diversion for other purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: County school funds and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Moneys and property belonging to a county school fund, and proceeds from sales of estrays, penalties, forfeitures, fines collected for penal/military law breaches, and payments in lieu of military duty shall belong to counties and be faithfully appropriated to free public schools; amounts collected in each county to be annually reported to Superintendent of Public Instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies county-level educational revenues, their permitted uses, and reporting obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: University trustees and benefits for youth
rubrics_metrics.description: General Assembly shall provide for election of Trustees of the University of North Carolina vested with its privileges and endowments and may make provisions necessary for maintenance and management; benefits of the University shall, as far as practicable, be extended to youth of the State free of expense for tuition; escheats and unclaimed dividends appropriated to University use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs legislative oversight of University governance and emphasizes tuition-free access where practicable with dedicated funding sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Board of Education composition and powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Governor, Lieutenant-Governor, Secretary of State, Treasurer, Auditor, Superintendent of Public Instruction and Attorney-General shall constitute a State Board of Education; Governor shall be President and Superintendent Secretary; Board shall succeed to powers of the Literary Fund and have full power to legislate rules for free public schools and educational fund, subject to alteration by General Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates executive-heavy Board with delegated rulemaking powers for education but subject to legislative override.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of Education procedures and expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: First session of Board to be held at State capitol within fifteen days after organization; majority constitutes quorum; contingent expenses of Board to be provided by General Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies procedural logistics, quorum, and funding responsibility for Board operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: University-connected departments and normal instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as practicable General Assembly shall establish and maintain in connection with the University departments of Agriculture, Mechanics, Mining, and Normal Instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires establishment of practical and teacher-training departments within the University framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory education provision
rubrics_metrics.description: General Assembly empowered to enact that every child of sufficient mental and physical ability shall attend public schools between ages six and eighteen for a term not less than sixteen months, unless educated by other means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizes compulsory attendance laws with minimum aggregate attendance requirement and exemption for alternate education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal property homestead exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal property of any resident to the value of five hundred dollars, to be selected by such resident, shall be exempt from sale under execution or other final process for collection of any debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a $500 personal property exemption from creditor execution, selectable by owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real property homestead exemption and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Every homestead and the dwellings and buildings used therewith not exceeding in value one thousand dollars, to be selected by the owner, or in lieu any lot in city/town/village with dwellings not exceeding $1,000, shall be exempt from sale under execution for debt; but not exempt from sale for taxes or obligations contracted for purchase of said premises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides homestead exemption up to $1,000 with exceptions for tax sale and purchase-mortgage obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homestead protection after owner's death
rubrics_metrics.description: The homestead after death of the owner shall be exempt from payment of any debt during the minority of his children or any one of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects homestead for minor children from creditor claims until majority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liens excepted from homestead exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections on homestead exemptions shall not prevent a laborer's lien for work done for the person claiming exemption or a mechanic's lien for work done on the premises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves valid labor and mechanic liens against homestead property despite exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Widow's homestead rights
rubrics_metrics.description: If owner of a homestead die leaving a widow but no children, the same shall be exempt from the debts of her husband and the rents and profits shall inure to her benefit during widowhood, unless she be the owner of a homestead in her own right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secures homestead income for surviving widow absent children, with caveat if she already owns a homestead.
